cleared.check: Part one. The runtime was rebuilt with solc 0.8.26 at the settings of foundry.toml and with an explicit copy of the default optimizer step sequence of v0.8.26; both runtimes equal research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json byte for byte. Every one of the 10,418 instructions was given a source location from the deployed source map and an owner: the selector switch (pc 0 to 389), the 33 external functions found by a static walk from their selector cases, 60 Yul functions with entry points from functionDebugData (fun_swap alone holds 1,682 instructions), ranges shared by several external functions, and the 8 trailing data bytes. The table is in research/network-risk/cycles/009/core-code-bytecode-map.work/bytecode-map.json (coarseRanges, perOwner) and research/network-risk/cycles/009/core-code-bytecode-map.work/table.json (2,394 fine ranges with the source function of each).
cleared.result: The map is complete and no instruction is without an owner. With the four script sets of OPCODES.md (rerun here with cov_full.py) 9,840 instructions execute and 578 in 32 runs do not. Each unexecuted run is named in bytecode-map.json uncoveredRuns. They are revert paths (ManagerLocked, NonzeroNativeValue, PriceLimitOutOfBounds, tick bound and tick spacing reverts, native transfer bubble up), hook paths (afterRemoveLiquidity and the self call returns at Hooks.sol:217, 253 and 293), the finite allowance branch of transferFrom (ERC6909.sol:36-38), dead code (SELFBALANCE at Currency.sol:92, bytes4 of short hook calldata at Hooks.sol:137, InvalidTick at TickMath.sol:70), arithmetic paths that always end in a SafeCast revert (amounts above type(uint160).max at SqrtPriceMath.sol:95-109 and the 512 bit branch of the fee mulDiv, which give results above 2^127 that Pool.sol:192, 455 and 459 reject), the price overflow fallback at SqrtPriceMath.sol:52, and the metadata.

cleared.check: Part two, all instances. Every MULMOD (13), SDIV (4), SMOD (3), SAR (19), BYTE (2 in code), DIV (22) and MOD (3) was matched to its source line, and the counts equal the counts of the same builtins in irOptimized one to one. 52 of the 66 sit in Yul functions that were entered directly at their entry point in the reference interpreter with chosen stacks (harness.py, fntests.py): 64,187 cases at the edges of OPCODES.md (limb borders, the sign bit, divisors 0, 1, 2^96, 2^128, 10^6 and 2^256-1, products that are multiples of 2^256-1, quotients within 2^129 of 2^256, negative ticks and tick spacings that do not divide them, int128 limits) and with random garbage above the low 24, 128 or 160 bits of every narrower argument.
cleared.result: No mismatch against floor or ceiling division, exact signed truncation toward zero with the remainder taking the sign of the dividend (flipTick reverts with TickMisaligned carrying the sign extended tick and spacing), the BYTE table lookups of BitMath, the SAR sign masks of absDiff and BalanceDelta, and the reverts the source asks for (zero denominator, result of 2^256 or more, SafeCast, int128 overflow). Narrower arguments are masked or sign extended before use (and 0xff..ff on uint160 and uint128, signextend 2 and 15), so dirty upper bits change no result. The other 14 (SMOD, SDIV, SAR in TickBitmap.compress and position inlined in fun_swap and the modifyLiquidity dispatcher, tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick, simpleMulDiv, divRoundingUp, the lsb DIV and BYTE) were read in irOptimized: operand order sdiv(tick, tickSpacing), smod(MIN_TICK, spacing), div(0xd76453e0, shr(r, x)) and div(shl(128, fee), liquidity) is as in TickBitmap.sol:24-26, Pool.sol:577-580, BitMath.sol:45 and UnsafeMath.sol:24-27.

cleared.check: Part two, sample of SIGNEXTEND, SLT, SGT, SHL and SHR: 103 instructions, at least one and usually two from each of the 67 source or Yul functions that hold one, listed with source line in bytecode-map.json part2_sample_sign_and_shift. Instances in tested Yul functions were checked by fntests.py; the others by reading irOptimized: Slot0 fields (tick signextend(2, shr(160, slot)), protocolFee shr 184 and 196 masked to 12 bits, lpFee shr 208 masked to 24 bits), the slot0 rewrite in Pool.swap that keeps bits 184 to 255, toBalanceDelta, checkTicks (Pool.sol:95-97), tick <= slot0.tick in updateTick, liquidityDelta >= 0 and < 0, amountSpecified > 0 and < 0, the tickNext clamps (Pool.sol:351-356), the tickBitmap word key signextend(1, sar(8, compressed)), and the masks of nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord.
cleared.result: Each width and shift amount equals the source: sign extension from byte 2 for int24 and byte 15 for int128, word position as int16, shift 128 for the BalanceDelta halves, 96 and 32 for the Q96 conversions. No comparison operator is inverted and no signed comparison became unsigned.

cleared.check: Places where the optimizer changed the form of the arithmetic, checked for every input.
cleared.result: Four constant clones of mulDiv: fun_mulDiv_40234 (denominator 2^128) returns shr(128, prod0 - rem) | shl(128, prod1 - borrow); fun_mulDiv_40437 (2^96) the same with 96 and 160; fun_mulDiv_40430 (10^6) multiplies (prod0 - rem) >> 6 | (prod1 - borrow) << 250 by 0xde8f6cef...68c26139, and 15625 times that constant is 1 mod 2^256 (checked in python), which is FullMath.sol:59-99 with twos = 64 folded; fun_mulDiv_40456 fixes b = Q96 and uses shl(96, a) for a * Q96 mod 2^256. getTickAtSqrtPrice computes f = shr(255, r*r) and the log bit as and(shr(192+i, r*r), 2^(63-i)), equal to shl(63-i, shr(128, shr(127, r*r))) because the square is below 2^256 (TickMath.sol:141-223). The lsb upper bits become and(shr(247, shl(and(shr(248, m), 252), C)), 480), equal to shl(5, shr(252, shl(shl(2, shr(250, m)), C))) (BitMath.sol:40). simpleMulDiv(x, Q128, L) became div(shl(128, x), L) (Pool.sol:405, 474, 477). All are identities over 256 bit words, and the clones also pass fntests.py.

cleared.check: Whole tick range through the compiled TickMath: for each of the 1,774,545 ticks the bytecode's getSqrtPriceAtTick equals the transcription of TickMath.sol:57-114 in tools/opdiff/v4math.py, prices strictly increase, getTickAtSqrtPrice of the price returns the tick and of the price minus one returns the tick below (fullrange.py).

cleared.check: Part three: the one EXP and the one ADDMOD.
cleared.result: Both are data. The runtime ends with 0xfe at pc 23996 followed by the CBOR metadata a164736f6c634300081a000a (solc 0.8.26), which a linear disassembly reads as LOG1, PUSH5, STOP, ADDMOD (0x08), BYTE (0x1a), STOP, EXP (0x0a). The source map has 10,410 entries and stops before them, the 0xfe follows an unconditional JUMP at pc 23995, and none of the 13 bytes is 0x5b, so no jump can land there. The code has no EXP and no ADDMOD, irOptimized has neither builtin, and the third BYTE, the only LOG1 and the only INVALID of the earlier opcode census are the same data bytes.

cleared.check: Whether the ruint 1.21.0 mul_mod fault described in OPCODES.md:120-136, which needs a modulus of four 64 bit limbs and a quotient of the product by the modulus within 2^129 of 2^256, can be reached by any MULMOD of this bytecode, for any input, on a node that runs that release.
cleared.result: No. Five MULMODs have the constant modulus 2^256-1 (four limbs), and the inputs of their callers bound the product: liquidity << 96 times a price difference or a price (2^384), a fee growth difference times liquidity (2^384), an amount times Q96 (2^352), an amount times a fee below 10^6, liquidity times a price difference (2^288). Their quotient is at most 2^128. Of the other eight, six have a modulus of at most three limbs: the constants 2^128, 2^96 and 10^6, liquidity (uint128), a sqrt price (uint160) and 10^6 minus the fee. The remaining two take n1 + product and n1 - product of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (SqrtPriceMath.sol:47 and 71), with a product n1 * sqrtPX96 below 2^384. A four limb modulus of at least 2^192 then leaves a quotient below 2^192. Both conditions of the fault never hold together in this code, whatever the input. This is stronger than the in-pool argument of OPCODES.md.

cleared.check: Solidity bug SOL-2026-7 YulOptimizerKnowledgeBaseStaleBookkeeping (introduced 0.8.19, fixed 0.8.38, conditions: Yul optimizer with LoadResolver L or EqualStoreEliminator E): a load replaced by a stale value or a needed store removed when two addresses derive from one variable before and after it is reassigned. The build uses 0.8.26 with via-IR and the default sequence, so it is in range.
cleared.result: The bug did not act on this build. Removing every E from the default sequence gives a byte identical runtime, and so does removing the first two of the three L. Only the third L (in CTUca[r]LSs) changes the output, and the build fails with stack too deep without it. Rerunning the Yul optimizer of the same compiler on the unoptimized IR up to that L and through it, with tstore and tload substituted by operations of the same storage and memory effect so that the Yul front end accepts the code, shows 32 replaced loads and no replaced keccak256. All of them read a location written or read just before on a straight path through an address with a base that is never reassigned: fields of the params struct at memPtr_2 + 32, 64 and 96 in the five modifyLiquidity copies, the step struct at memPtr_1 + 32 in Pool.swap, the free memory pointer at 0x40 around events, and owner slot 0 in transferOwnership and onlyOwner. The loads after the tick clamps in Pool.swap stay in the final IR. The same reproduction with the full sequence gives the IR of the build up to clone names.

cleared.check: The other bugs that bugs_by_version.json lists for 0.8.26 (OverlappingRecursiveStorageStructCopyCorruption and its via-IR twin, MisorderedNamedParametersInRequireWithCustomErrors, MemoryByteArrayElementDeleteClearsWholeWord, SpillSlotCollisionAcrossMutualRecursion, UnsoundSpillInMutualRecursion, LostStorageArrayWriteOnSlotOverflow).
cleared.result: None applies. src/ has no recursive struct and no storage array; its four require calls take no custom error (FullMath.sol:30, 113, BitMath.sol:13, 32); the byte array delete bug is in the evmasm pipeline only; the two spill bugs need mutual recursion, and the call graph of the 66 runtime Yul functions has no cycle. The stack limit evader did move one variable to memory (memoryguard(0xa0), one mstore(0x80, ..) holding the pool state slot in modifyLiquidity, 19 reads), and no assembly in src/ writes memory between 0x60 and 0xa0 except on paths that revert.

Dead code. Its only callers are sync (PoolManager.sol:281-285) and _settle (PoolManager.sol:353-359), both of which branch away when the currency is address(0); the compiled settle tests the masked synced currency before calling. The native balance is never read by the PoolManager, so a network with a different SELFBALANCE or native balance face cannot change settlement through this instruction.

leads.question: Before Monad validators adopt v0.16.6, does its new compiled path for a constant shifted by a variable amount give the specified result for the six such shifts in this bytecode: SHL of 1 by and(tick, 0xff) at pc 16691 (TickBitmap.sol:73) and pc 21183 (TickBitmap.sol:110), SHR of 2^256-1 by 255 - bitPos at pc 19356 (TickBitmap.sol:97), SHL of the 256 bit lsb table by 0 to 252 at pc 21364 (BitMath.sol:40), SHR of the 128 bit msb table 0x8421084210842108cc6318c6db6d54be by 1 to 255 at pc 23648 (BitMath.sol:22), and SHL of a bytes4 mask at pc 16643 (dead)?
leads.why: These shapes decide the tick bitmap words and the bit scans in every swap and liquidity change. A compiled result that differs for shift amounts of 128 or more on a two limb constant would move the price to a wrong tick or skip initialized ticks, and simulated calls cannot reach compiled code, so only a reading or mined swaps would show it. The operand list is in operands.json of the work directory.

leads.question: If the deployer rebuilds with Solidity 0.8.38 or later to leave the SOL-2026-7 range, is the runtime byte identical to this build, and if not, do the four script sets, fntests.py and fullrange.py still pass on the new bytecode?
leads.why: This review cleared the 0.8.26 build only. A different compiler gives a different bytecode, and all network comparisons of OPCODES.md were made with the 0.8.26 bytes.
